operations.description:
List and search tasks within the organization with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities.

Retrieves tasks that match the provided search criteria. Supports filtering by status (TODO, IN_PROGRESS, IN_REVIEW, DONE), priority (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL), project assignment, assigned employee, due date range, and creation date range.

Users can paginate through results with cursor-based pagination for efficient large result set handling. Tasks are organization-isolated; users only see tasks from their currently selected organization context.

Hierarchical task queries can retrieve child tasks by specifying a parent task ID. Results include summary information optimized for list display, with full details available via the task at endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_tasks table with organization isolation (org_id from user context).

Apply search filters from requestBody:
- status: filter by exact status (TODO, IN_PROGRESS, IN_REVIEW, DONE)
- priority: filter by exact priority (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)
- project_id: filter by project
- assigned_employee_id: filter by assigned employee
- parent_task_id: filter child tasks by parent (hierarchical query)
- due_date_after, due_date_before: date range filter
- created_after, created_before: creation date range filter
- title: partial match search on title field using trigram index

Apply sorting from requestBody (sortBy, sortOrder):
- sortBy options: created_at, updated_at, due_date, priority, title
- sortOrder options: ASC, DESC

Apply pagination from requestBody:
- limit: maximum 100 items per page
- cursor: last task ID from previous page for cursor-based pagination

Return IPageIHrmPlatformTask.ISummary with:
- items: array of task summaries (excluded: description, parent_task details, children_tasks array to prevent circular references)
- totalCount: total matching count
- nextCursor: cursor for next page (null if last page)

Enforce organization data isolation: only return tasks where project belongs to user's organization (via project_id join with hrm_platform_projects where project.org_id matches user's org_id).

Return 404 if organization context not found (edge case).
Log task list access for audit trail (activity logging).

Handle edge cases:
- Empty result set: return paginated response with empty items array
- No filters provided: return all tasks for user's organization
- Invalid filter values: reject with 400 error
- Invalid sort field: default to created_at ASC

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task summary records optimized for administrative task list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status, priority, project, employee, date range filters, sorting, and pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single task by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete task entity including title, description, status, priority, assignment details, and timestamps. The task must belong to a project that the requesting user has view access to. If the task does not exist or the user lacks permission, the request is rejected.

The task entity includes hierarchical information (parent and children tasks), assigned employee details if applicable, project context, and all relevant metadata for task management operations.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch hrm_platform_tasks record by id from database.

1. Query hrm_platform_tasks where id = {taskId}
2. Verify task exists and deleted_at is null (not soft-deleted)
3. Verify user has project:view permission for task's project_id
4. If user has project:view permission, return task with full entity:
   - Include all task fields: id, project_id, parent_task_id, assigned_employee_id, title, description, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
   - Include related entities: project (id, name), parentTask (if exists, full entity), childrenTasks (array of child task summaries), assignedEmployee (if assigned, employee summary with name and email)
5. If task not found or user lacks permission, return 404 Not Found

Edge cases:
- Task with parent_task_id: Load and include parent task entity
- Task with children: Load and include only summary fields for children (id, title, status, due_date) to prevent excessive data
- Unassigned task (assigned_employee_id = null): Return task without employee relationship
- Task belongs to different project: Check user's project membership or role-based project:view permission before returning

Validation:
- taskId must be valid UUID format
- rejected: 404 if task does not exist or is soft-deleted
- rejected: 403 if user lacks project:view permission for the task's project

responseBody.description: Complete task entity with all fields and related relationships including project context, parent task (if exists), child tasks (summaries), and assigned employee (if assigned).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task to retrieve (global scope)
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Create a new task within a project for work tracking and assignment.

Creates a task with a unique identifier, associated with a project. Project leads or users with project management permissions can create tasks. The task title is required; description, priority, estimated hours, and due date are optional. Tasks can be created as root tasks or subtasks (max one level of nesting).

The system validates user permissions against the target project before creation. Unauthorized users are denied without access to project context.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate user has permission to create tasks in project (project lead or project management permission per section 508)
2. Validate task title is provided and non-empty
3. Validate if parent_task_id is provided, parent exists, belongs to same project, and is a root task (no existing children with parent to enforce single nesting level)
4. Validate if assigned_employee_id is provided, employee belongs to same organization as project
5. Set status to TODO (default new task status)
6. Set priority to MEDIUM (default priority) if not provided
7. Create task record with auto-generated UUID for id
8. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
9. Return full task object including computed relationships

responseBody.description: The created task with all fields including system-generated id, timestamps, and default values.

requestBody.description: Task creation data including title, description, project association, and optional fields for assignment, priority, estimated hours, and due date.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before a task can be created because task.project_id is a required foreign key reference to hrm_platform_projects. Each task belongs to exactly one project.

operations.description:
Update an existing task with new attributes.

This operation allows authorized users to modify task properties including title, description, status, priority, assignment, estimated hours, and due date. The user must have project lead role or project management permission in the project associated with the task.

Only specific fields can be modified: title, description, status, priority, assigned_employee_id, estimated_hours, and due_date. The project_id is immutable after task creation.

Status transitions follow the workflow: TODO → IN_PROGRESS → IN_REVIEW → DONE. Transitions are validated and tracked in the task history table.

The operation returns the complete updated task object including all fields.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that taskId is a valid UUID format.
2. Query hrm_platform_tasks table to find the task by id.
3. If task not found, return 404 Not Found error.
4. Check soft deletion: if deleted_at is not null, return 404 Not Found error.
5. Query the project_id from the task record.
6. Verify user authorization:
   - Check if user has project management permission in the project, OR
   - Check if user is assigned as project lead in hrm_platform_project_memberships for this project
   - If not authorized, return 403 Forbidden error.
7. Validate any status transition against allowed workflow (TODO → IN_PROGRESS → IN_REVIEW → DONE).
8. Update only provided fields in the request body:
   - title: update if provided (required field in DB)
   - description: update if provided
   - status: update if provided (validate workflow transition)
   - priority: update if provided (validate allowed values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)
   - assigned_employee_id: update if provided (validate employee exists in same organization)
   - estimated_hours: update if provided (must be >= 0)
   - due_date: update if provided
9. Set updated_at timestamp to current time.
10. Save changes to database.
11. Create task history entry in hrm_platform_task_histories table with old and new values for changed fields.
12. Return the complete updated task object.

Error cases:
- 404: Task not found or already deleted
- 403: User not authorized to modify this task
- 400: Invalid status transition, invalid priority value, invalid employee ID, estimated_hours < 0, or task_id not matching path parameter

responseBody.description: The complete updated task with all fields including read-only system fields like created_at and updated_at.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task to update.
parameters.name: taskId

requestBody.description: Task fields to update. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates. The project_id cannot be changed after task creation.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a task and all its associated history.

This operation removes a task from the system along with all its task history entries via cascade deletion. Child tasks (subtasks) are also deleted, including their history.

**Authorization**: Requires `project:manage` permission on the project that owns the task.

**Irreversible**: Deleted tasks cannot be recovered. This is a permanent deletion with no undo functionality.

**Cascade**: All task history entries for the deleted task are automatically removed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Verify user is authenticated and has project:manage permission for the project that owns the task.
2. Look up the task by taskId from hrm_platform_tasks.
3. If task not found or deleted_at is not null, return 404 Not Found.
4. Verify the task is owned by the current organization context.
5. Delete the task record from hrm_platform_tasks.
6. Cascade delete all associated hrm_platform_task_histories (handled by database ON DELETE CASCADE).
7. Cascade delete all child tasks (recursive deletion).
8. Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

**Error handling**:
- 404: Task not found or already deleted
- 403: User lacks project:manage permission
- 400: Task has assigned timelogs (if business rule requires)
- 500: Database constraint violations or cascade failures

parameters.description: UUID of the task to delete.
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Search and list task history entries with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities.

Retrieves a paginated list of task history records that document status changes, assignments, and other modifications made to tasks. Each history entry captures when a change occurred, what changed, and who made the modification.

This endpoint supports filtering by task ID, member who made the change, action type, date ranges, and status transitions. Results can be sorted by change timestamp, action type, or task reference. The operation is read-only as history entries are immutable audit records.

All history entries include the task reference, actor attribution, action category, and timestamps for both when the change occurred and when the entry was created.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_task_histories table with pagination and filtering.

1. Apply filters from requestBody:
   - task_id: Filter by specific task ID
   - actor_id: Filter by member who made the change
   - action_type: Filter by action type (status_change, assignment_change, title_change, description_change, priority_change, parent_change, due_date_change, start_date_change)
   - changed_at_gte: Filter entries changed on or after this timestamp
   - changed_at_lte: Filter entries changed on or before this timestamp
   - status_before: Filter entries where previous status matches (requires action_type=status_change)
   - status_after: Filter entries where new status matches (requires action_type=status_change)
   - Deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from results.

2. Apply sorting:
   - Default sort: changed_at DESC (most recent changes first)
   - Allow sorting by: changed_at, created_at, action_type, task_id
   - Allow sort order: asc, desc

3. Apply pagination:
   - Use cursor-based pagination with pageToken for next/previous navigation
   - Default page size: 20 records
   - Maximum page size: 100 records
   - Return cursor tokens for next and previous pages

4. Join with hrm_platform_tasks to include task reference data (task_id, task title if available)
   - Join with hrm_platform_members to include actor reference data (actor_id, actor email if available)

5. Return paginated response with:
   - Array of task history summary records
   - Pagination metadata (pageToken, hasNext, hasPrevious, totalCount)
   - Record each history entry with: id, task_id, actor_id, action_type, status_before, status_after, details, changed_at, created_at

6. Error handling:
   - Return 400 if invalid filter parameters are provided
   - Return 400 if status_before/status_after filters are used without action_type=status_change
   - Return 400 if pageToken is invalid or corrupted
   - Return empty array with pagination metadata if no matching records

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task history summary records with pagination metadata. Each record contains the history entry ID, task reference, actor reference, action type, status transitions (if applicable), change details, and timestamps. Pagination includes cursor tokens for next and previous page navigation.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for task history entries including filter parameters, sorting options, and pagination settings. All filters are optional. When no filters are provided, returns all history entries (non-deleted) with default pagination and sorting.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task history entry by its unique identifier.

Returns the complete audit record for a specific task status change or modification, including the timestamp of the change, the user who made it, the previous and new status values (if applicable), and the action type. This operation is used when reviewing the detailed history of a particular change event.

### Response Fields

The response includes all fields stored in the task history record:
- **id**: Unique identifier of the history entry
- **task_id**: Reference to the task that was changed
- **actor_id**: Reference to the member who made the change
- **action_type**: Category of change (status_change, assignment_change, title_change, etc.)
- **status_before**: Previous status value (for status changes)
- **status_after**: New status value (for status changes)
- **details**: Additional structured change data in JSON format
- **changed_at**: Timestamp when the change was applied to the task
- **created_at**: Timestamp when this history record was created
- **updated_at**: Timestamp of the last modification to this record

### Access Control

Users can only view task history entries for tasks they have permission to access. If the task is not accessible to the user, the system returns a 404 Not Found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve task history entry by UUID from hrm_platform_task_histories table.

### Implementation Steps:

1. Parse and validate the historyId path parameter as a valid UUID.

2. Query the hrm_platform_task_histories table where:
   - id = {historyId}
   - deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted records)

3. If no record is found, return 404 Not Found.

4. Verify that the user has permission to view this history entry by checking access to the associated task (hrm_platform_tasks).
   - If the user cannot view the associated task, return 404 Not Found (do not reveal the history entry exists)

5. Join with related tables for complete context:
   - hrm_platform_tasks (for task details if needed in response)
   - hrm_platform_members (for actor/user information if needed in response)

6. Return the full task history entity including all fields:
   - id, task_id, actor_id, action_type, status_before, status_after, details, changed_at, created_at, updated_at

### Edge Cases:

- **History entry not found**: Return 404 if the historyId does not exist or has been soft-deleted.
- **No permission**: Return 404 if the user lacks access to the associated task (hide existence of history entry).
- **Task deleted**: If the associated task has been deleted, still return the history entry as it represents historical audit data. The history is independent of the task's existence.
- **Soft delete**: If deleted_at is not NULL, the history entry should not be returned (treat as 404).

### Error Responses:

- **404 Not Found**: History entry does not exist, has been soft-deleted, or user lacks permission to view the associated task.
- **400 Bad Request**: Invalid UUID format in historyId path parameter.

responseBody.description: Complete task history entry including all audit details such as the action type, status transitions, change timestamp, and user attribution.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task history entry to retrieve.
parameters.name: historyId

operations.description:
Search and list timer records for the authenticated employee with optional filters and pagination.

This endpoint enables employees to browse their own timer history and currently active timers. The search supports filtering by timer status (started, paused, stopped), date ranges (created_at, last_tick_at), project and task associations, and organization context. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large result sets.

The endpoint enforces strict ownership boundaries - employees can only access timers they own through authentication. Status filtering allows viewing active (started/paused) timers separately from historical (stopped) timers. Optional project and task filters enable time tracking analysis across different work items.

Sorting is available by creation date, last update timestamp, or elapsed duration to support different browsing preferences.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timers table with pagination and filtering.

1. Validate employee authentication and extract employee_id from session
2. Apply all optional filters from requestBody:
   - status: Filter by timer status (started, paused, stopped) - enum validation required
   - project_id: hrm_platform_project_id filter (UUID or null)
   - task_id: hrm_platform_task_id filter (UUID or null)
   - date ranges: created_at range, last_tick_at range for time boundaries
3. Build cursor-based pagination:
   - Accept cursor from previous response for pagination continuation (ISO datetime timestamp)
   - Return nextCursor in response for navigation
   - Default page size: 20, max page size: 100, enforced via requestBody
4. Apply sorting per sortField and sortOrder:
   - sortField: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'durationSeconds', 'status', 'lastTickAt'
   - sortOrder: 'asc' or 'desc'
   - Default sort: createdAt descending (newest first)
5. Calculate elapsed time for active timers:
   - For started/paused timers: compute current elapsed time from last_tick_at to now
   - For stopped timers: use stored duration_seconds value
6. Filter by soft-delete: Exclude records where deleted_at is not null
7. Join with hrm_platform_projects and hrm_platform_tasks for project/task details in response (optional)
8. Return paginated result with:
   - timers: Array of timer summaries
   - pagination: { hasNextCursor, nextCursor }
9. Handle edge cases:
   - No results: Return empty array with null nextCursor
   - Invalid cursor: Return 400 Bad Request
   - Employee not found: Return 401 Unauthorized
   - Invalid status value: Return 400 Bad Request

Error handling:
- 400: Invalid cursor format, invalid sort field, invalid status value, page size out of range
- 401: Unauthorized - employee not authenticated
- 404: Employee record not found in database

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer summary records optimized for employee timer browsing and time tracking analysis. Each timer includes status, calculated elapsed time, project and task associations, and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and sorting timer records. Includes status filters, date range constraints, project and task associations, pagination parameters, and sorting configuration. All filters are optional and can be combined for precise querying. Page size defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timer record by its unique identifier, returning full timer details including current status, elapsed time, project and task associations.

Returns the complete timer object including id, employee reference, associated project and task, current status, timestamps, and calculated duration. The operation validates that the requesting employee is the owner of the timer (hrm_platform_employee_id match).

Only active and stopped timers are returned. Soft-deleted timers (where deleted_at is not null) are not accessible.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate timerId is a valid UUID format
2. Query hrm_platform_timers table WHERE id = timerId AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
4. Verify authentication: check that the authenticated employee's id matches hrm_platform_employee_id
   - If mismatch, return 403 Forbidden (employees can only view their own timers)
5. Verify employee is active (not deactivated)
6. Return full timer record with all fields including:
   - id, hrm_platform_employee_id, hrm_platform_project_id, hrm_platform_task_id
   - status, duration_seconds, last_tick_at, created_at, updated_at
   - Include related project and task data if referenced
7. Calculate and include elapsed_time_seconds based on current time if status is 'started'

responseBody.description: Full timer record with all details including id, status, duration, project and task associations, and timestamps.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the timer to retrieve.
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Create a new timer to start tracking time for a project or task.

Creates a new timer record with status set to 'started'. The timer can be optionally associated with a project and/or task. Once created, the timer begins accumulating elapsed time automatically.

Only active employees can create timers. The system validates that the employee exists, is active, and has not exceeded any concurrent timer limits (only one active timer per employee allowed).
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract employee_id from authentication context (active member session)
2. Validate employee exists and status is 'active' (per ID 485, 487 requirements)
3. Check employee has no other active timer (started or paused status) - reject if exists (per ID 482)
4. Validate optional hrm_platform_project_id and hrm_platform_task_id if provided:
   - Project must exist and belong to same organization as employee
   - Task must exist, belong to same project, and belong to same organization
5. Create timer with:
   - id: generate new UUID
   - hrm_platform_employee_id: from auth context
   - hrm_platform_project_id: from request body (optional)
   - hrm_platform_task_id: from request body (optional)
   - status: 'started'
   - duration_seconds: 0
   - last_tick_at: current UTC timestamp
   - created_at: current UTC timestamp
   - updated_at: current UTC timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
6. Return full timer object with all fields

responseBody.description: The newly created timer with all fields including generated id, timestamps, and calculated elapsed time.

requestBody.description: Timer creation parameters including optional project and task associations.

operations.description:
Update an existing timer record with new project, task, and description information.

This operation allows an employee to modify their active timer's associated project and task, as well as the timer description. The timer must belong to the authenticated employee and cannot be in a stopped state. Modified fields include the description, project, and task associations; system-managed fields such as id, timestamps, and duration are read-only and will not be updated.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated employee owns this timer (hrm_platform_employee_id matches)
2. Validate timer exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
3. Validate timer is not in 'stopped' status - stopped timers are immutable
4. Validate description is provided if included (optional string field)
5. Validate project_id and task_id references (if provided) exist and belong to the employee's organization
6. Update the timer record with new description, hrm_platform_project_id, and hrm_platform_task_id values
7. Set updated_at to current timestamp
8. Return the updated full timer record
9. If validation fails, return 400 with appropriate error message
10. If timer not found, return 404
11. If employee does not own the timer, return 403

responseBody.description: The updated full timer record including all fields after modification.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer to update.
parameters.name: timerId

requestBody.description: Timer update data. Allowed fields: description (optional string), hrm_platform_project_id (optional), hrm_platform_task_id (optional). System-managed fields are read-only.

operations.description:
Delete a timer by setting its deletion timestamp.

This operation performs a soft delete on the timer record, preserving historical data for audit and timesheet purposes. The employee can only delete timers they own. Timer status (started, paused, or stopped) is accepted but does not affect the deletion process.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate timerId is a valid UUID
2. Query hrm_platform_timers for the timer record
3. Verify ownership: hrm_platform_employee_id must match the authenticated employee's ID
4. Set deleted_at to current timestamp (soft delete)
5. Return the deleted timer record with updated deleted_at value
6. Throw 404 if timer not found
7. Throw 403 if timer belongs to different employee
8. Handle cascade deletes for related records via foreign key constraints

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer to delete. This is the primary key (UUID) of the timer record.
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Search and retrieve timelogs with pagination, filtering, and sorting options.

Retrieves timelogs with support for filtering by employee, project, task, date ranges, billable status, and organization context. Supports cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large result sets.

Returns paginated timelog summaries with essential fields for list displays. Full timelog details can be retrieved individually via GET /timelogs/{id}.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timelogs table with the following implementation steps:

1. Authentication: Verify user is authenticated and has appropriate organization context.

2. Organization Filtering: If the user is not a time manager, automatically filter timelogs by their organization's employees only.

3. Build Query:
   - Apply filters from request body:
     * employee_id: Filter by specific employee
     * project_id: Filter by specific project
     * task_id: Filter by specific task
     * start_date: Filter timelogs where start_datetime >= start_date
     * end_date: Filter timelogs where end_datetime <= end_date
     * billable: Filter by billable status (true/false)
     * status: Filter timelogs not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   
4. Pagination:
   - Use cursor-based pagination
   - Default page size: 20 items
   - Maximum page size: 100 items
   - Sort by created_at descending by default
   - Support sorting by: created_at, start_datetime, end_datetime, duration_minutes
   
5. Join Requirements:
   - Join with hrm_platform_employees to verify employee ownership
   - Join with hrm_platform_projects for project context (if needed)
   - Join with hrm_platform_tasks for task context (if requested)

6. Response Construction:
   - Return paginated list with cursor metadata (nextCursor, hasNextPage)
   - Include total count for pagination UI
   - Return timelog summary fields only (id, employee_id, project_id, task_id, start_datetime, end_datetime, duration_minutes, billable, description)

7. Error Handling:
   - 400: Invalid pagination parameters (page size out of range)
   - 400: Invalid date range (end_date < start_date)
   - 403: Attempting to access timelogs outside user's organization scope
   - 404: Requested employee/project/task does not exist

8. Authorization Rules:
   - Employees can view their own timelogs
   - Time managers with appropriate permissions can view all timelogs in organization
   - Owner can view all timelogs across organization

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timelog summary records for efficient list displays.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including employee filter, project filter, date range filters, billable status, pagination parameters, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog by its unique identifier.

Fetches the complete timelog record including all details such as employee, project, task, timestamps, duration, description, and billable status. Returns 404 if the timelog does not exist or has been soft-deleted.

Authorization: Employees can view their own timelogs. Users with time:view_all permission can view any timelog in the organization. If the user lacks permission, returns 404 to avoid information leakage.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single timelog by UUID from hrm_platform_timelogs table.

1. Validate timelogId is a valid UUID format
2. Query hrm_platform_timelogs where id = timelogId AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Check authorization:
   - If user is employee and timelog.employee_id == user.employee_id → allow
   - If user has time:view_all permission in organization → allow
   - Otherwise, return 404 (not found) to avoid information leakage
4. Join with hrm_platform_employees, hrm_platform_projects, and hrm_platform_tasks to include full entity details
5. Return 404 if timelog not found or user lacks permission
6. Response includes all fields: id, employee_id, project_id, task_id, start_datetime, end_datetime, duration_minutes, description, billable, created_at, updated_at

responseBody.description: The complete timelog record with all details including associated employee, project, task references, timestamps, duration, description, and billable status.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timelog to retrieve
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry to record work performed on a project and task.

Creates a timelog entry that captures a work session with start/end times, duration, and project context. The timelog is automatically associated with the employee's current timesheet if it falls within the same week period.

### Business Rules

- Timelogs can only be added to draft timesheets. Once a timesheet is submitted or approved, timelogs cannot be added.
- The system validates that the work duration is positive and the datetime range is logical (end datetime after start datetime).
- If a timesheet exists for the week, the timelog is automatically included in that timesheet.
- The operation requires the employee to belong to the organization and the project to be active within that organization.
- Billable flag determines whether the work can be charged to clients.

### Authorization

- Only employees can create timelogs for their own work.
- Users with time:manage permission can create timelogs on behalf of other employees.

### Error Handling

Returns 400 Bad Request when:
- Timelog would violate timesheet immutability (timesheet is submitted or approved)
- Invalid datetime range (end before start, future dates not allowed)
- Duration is zero or negative
- Project does not exist or is not active
- Employee does not belong to the organization

Returns 403 Forbidden when the user lacks permission to create timelogs.

Returns 404 Not Found when the referenced employee, project, or task does not exist.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate request body fields:
   - Ensure employee_id exists and belongs to the user's organization (or user has time:manage permission)
   - Verify project_id exists and belongs to the same organization as the employee
   - If task_id is provided, verify it belongs to the same project
   - Validate start_datetime is in the past (no future timelogs)
   - Validate end_datetime is after start_datetime and in the past
   - Calculate duration_minutes = (end_datetime - start_datetime) in minutes; must be > 0
   - Validate billable is a boolean

2. Check timesheet status for the week period (start_datetime to end_datetime):
   - Find the employee's timesheet that contains the week period
   - If timesheet exists and status is 'submitted' or 'approved', return 400 error
   - If timesheet exists and status is 'draft' or 'rejected', allow addition
   - If no timesheet exists, create a new timelog (timesheet association will happen later)

3. Create timelog record:
   - Insert new record into hrm_platform_timelogs with all validated fields
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to null (active record)

4. Return the created timelog with full details including:
   - All fields from the created record
   - Joined project name and color code
   - Joined task title if task_id is present
   - Employee display name

5. If a timesheet was found and is in draft status, the timelog should be associated with it (this may happen via trigger or separate operation)

Edge cases:
- Multiple timelogs can be created for the same task/project in the same week
- Timelogs can overlap with existing timelogs (system does not prevent this)
- If project is archived or completed, timelogs can still be created for historical tracking

responseBody.description: The newly created timelog entry with full details including associated project and task information.

requestBody.description: Timelog creation data including employee assignment, project and task context, work session times, duration, description, and billable flag.

prerequisites.description: Project must exist before timelogs can be logged against it. The operation validates project_id exists and belongs to the employee's organization.
If task_id is provided in the request, the task must exist and belong to the same project. This is a conditional prerequisite when a specific task is being referenced.

operations.description:
Update an existing timelog entry by its unique identifier.

This operation allows employees to modify their own time entries, including project/task associations, timing details, duration, and billable status. Updates are subject to business constraints: the timelog must belong to the authenticated employee, the associated project must not be in 'completed' status (per business rule #604), and if the timelog is part of a submitted or approved timesheet, it cannot be modified (per business rule #139).

Successful updates return the complete updated timelog with all fields including system-managed timestamps.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate timelogId is a valid UUID format.
2. Retrieve timelog from hrm_platform_timelogs where id = timelogId.
3. If not found, return 404 Not Found.
4. Validate authenticated member's employee record: query hrm_platform_employees where user_id = authenticated_member.user_id AND organization_id = current_org_context.
5. Verify employee_id of timelog matches authenticated employee.id. If mismatch, return 403 Forbidden (per business rule #444).
6. Check if timelog.deleted_at is not null. If soft-deleted, return 400 Bad Request.
7. Verify project status: join with hrm_platform_projects on project_id. If project.status = 'completed', return 409 Conflict (per business rule #604).
8. Check timesheet immutability: query hrm_platform_timesheet_timelogs for any association with this timelog. Join with hrm_platform_timesheets on timesheet_id. If any associated timesheet has status != 'draft' (i.e., 'submitted', 'approved'), return 409 Conflict (per business rule #139 and #99).
9. If request contains project_id, verify project belongs to same organization as employee.
10. If request contains task_id, verify task belongs to the specified project.
11. Calculate duration_minutes from provided start_datetime and end_datetime: (end_datetime - start_datetime) in minutes. Validate end_datetime >= start_datetime.
12. Apply updates to timelog: set fields from IHrmPlatformTimelog.IUpdate, set updated_at = now().
13. Save timelog to database.
14. Query updated timelog with employee, project, and task relationships.
15. Return 200 OK with full timelog object.

responseBody.description: The complete updated timelog entry with all fields including system-managed metadata.

parameters.description: The UUID identifier of the timelog to update.
parameters.name: timelogId

requestBody.description: Timelog fields to update. At least one field must be provided. Fields excluded from update: id, employee_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a timelog entry from the system.

Deletes a timelog record by marking it with a deletion timestamp. The timelog remains in the database but is excluded from active queries.

**Deletion Permissions**:

- Employees can delete their own timelogs only if not associated with submitted or approved timesheets
- Users with `time:manage` permission can delete any employee's timelogs regardless of timesheet status
- Timelogs in draft or rejected timesheets can be deleted by the owning employee
- Timelogs in submitted or approved timesheets are protected from deletion

**Protected Operations**:

The system prevents deletion when a timelog is referenced by a timesheet in submitted or approved status. Users without time management permissions cannot bypass this restriction.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement soft-delete by setting deleted_at timestamp to current time.

**Authorization**:
1. Verify user is authenticated
2. If user has time:manage permission, allow deletion of any timelog
3. Otherwise, verify timelog.employee_id equals authenticated user's ID
4. Reject with 403 if permission check fails

**Timesheet Validation**:
1. Query timesheet_timelogs junction table for associations
2. For each associated timesheet, check status in timesheets table
3. If timesheet status is 'submitted' or 'approved', reject with 409 conflict
4. Allow deletion if no timesheet association or timesheet is 'draft' or 'rejected'

**Business Rules**:
- Preserve all historical timelog data (no cascade delete to timesheets or activity logs)
- Maintain referential integrity with project, task, and employee references
- Log deletion in activity_logs with action='timelog.delete'

**Error Responses**:
- 404 Not Found: Timelog does not exist or was already deleted
- 403 Forbidden: User lacks permission to delete this timelog
- 409 Conflict: Timelog is part of a submitted or approved timesheet
- 404 Not Found: Associated project, task, or employee not found (cascade constraint)

**Implementation Notes**:
- Use database transaction to ensure deleted_at is set atomically
- After deletion, timelog should be excluded from all standard queries via deleted_at filter
- Return full timelog object with deleted_at timestamp set to confirm successful deletion

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the timelog to delete
parameters.name: timelogId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timesheets with search filters and sorting options.

This endpoint provides administrative and user-facing access to timesheet records with support for filtering by status, date ranges, and employee. Results are paginated for efficient browsing of large datasets. Users can sort results by various fields including start date, status, or total hours.

Timesheet access follows ownership rules: employees can only view their own timesheets, while managers and organization owners can view all timesheets based on their permissions. The endpoint supports filtering by status values: pending, submitted, approved, rejected, or cancelled.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timesheets table with pagination and filtering.

Pagination:
- Support page number and page size parameters
- Return total count and pagination metadata
- Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination for large datasets

Filtering:
- Filter by status: pending, submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled (optional array filter)
- Filter by date range: start_date between start and end parameters
- Filter by employee_id: optional single employee ID filter for employee users
- Apply ownership validation: employees can only filter by their own employee_id

Sorting:

- Default sort by start_date descending (most recent weeks first)
- Allow ascending/descending order

Authorization:
- Check user role: employee users can only view their own timesheets
- Manager/owner users can view all timesheets in the organization
- Filter by hrm_platform_employee_id if user is employee

Response:
- Return paginated results with hrm_platform_timesheet summary data
- Include hrm_platform_employee reference for each timesheet
- Calculate or retrieve total_hours from timelogs if not precomputed
- Return pagination metadata: page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages

Edge Cases:

- Return 404 if requested employee_id doesn't exist (for employee user validation)

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timesheet by ID with complete details including employee information and associated timelogs.

## Access Control

This operation enforces strict access control based on user roles:

- **Timesheet Owner**: Employees can view their own timesheets regardless of status (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected).
- **Manager/Owner**: Managers and organization owners can view all timesheets within their organization for approval and oversight purposes.
- **Unauthorized Access**: Returns 403 Forbidden for users without proper authorization.

## Response Content

The response includes the complete timesheet record with:

- **Basic Information**: Timesheet ID, week period (start_date, end_date), current status
- **Workflow Timestamps**: submitted_at, approved_at, rejected_at, cancelled_at timestamps
- **Aggregated Data**: Total hours calculated from all included timelogs
- **Employee Information**: The owner of the timesheet
- **Timelogs**: All timelog entries included in this timesheet with project, task, and duration details
- **Status History**: Full workflow status progression for audit purposes
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a single timesheet by ID from hrm_platform_timesheets table.

Query the timesheet record where id = timesheetId parameter.

Authorization checks:

Include related data:
- Employee information from hrm_platform_employees

Apply soft delete filter: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Return full timesheet entity with all fields including:
- id, hrm_platform_employee_id, start_date, end_date
- status, submitted_at, approved_at, rejected_at, cancelled_at
- notes, total_hours
- created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
- Related employee object
- Array of timelog objects from timelogs relation

Handle not found: Return 404 if timesheet doesn't exist or is soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Create a new timesheet record for tracking work hours across a specific week period.

A timesheet represents a collection of timelogs grouped by week for submission and approval workflow. This operation initializes a new timesheet in pending status, which the employee can then populate with timelogs before submitting for manager review.

Only employees can create timesheets for themselves. The timesheet must cover a complete work week (Monday to Sunday). Once created in pending status, the timesheet can be modified until it is submitted for approval.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timesheet record in hrm_platform_timesheets table.

1. Validate that start_date represents a Monday and end_date represents a Sunday of the same week.
2. Validate that end_date is exactly 6 days after start_date (7-day week).
3. Verify hrm_platform_employee_id references an existing employee record.
4. Set status to 'pending' (equivalent to draft state in business logic).
5. Set submitted_at, approved_at, rejected_at, cancelled_at to NULL.
6. Set total_hours to NULL (will be calculated from associated timelogs).
7. Set notes to the provided value or NULL if not provided.
8. Generate a new UUID for the id field.
9. Set created_at and updated_at to the current timestamp.
10. Set deleted_at to NULL (record is active).
11. Return the complete created timesheet record.

Error cases:
- Return 400 if start_date and end_date don't form a valid week.
- Return 404 if hrm_platform_employee_id references a non-existent employee.
- Return 409 if a timesheet already exists for this employee covering the same week period (based on @@unique([hrm_platform_employee_id, start_date]) constraint).
- Return 403 if the requesting user doesn't have permission to create timesheets for this employee.

responseBody.description: The newly created timesheet record with all generated fields and initial status.

requestBody.description: Timesheet creation data including employee assignment, week period, and optional notes.

operations.description:
Update an existing timesheet record with new notes or other editable fields.

This operation allows the timesheet owner or users with time approval permissions to modify timesheet details while the timesheet is in pending or rejected status. Submitted and approved timesheets are locked and cannot be modified through this endpoint.

Only the notes field can be updated through this operation. Timesheet status transitions (submission, approval, rejection, cancellation) are handled through separate workflow operations. Once a timesheet is approved, its timelogs become permanently locked and cannot be modified.

The operation validates that the authenticated user has appropriate permissions (owner or manager with time approval) and that the timesheet is in a modifiable state before applying changes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve timesheet by ID from hrm_platform_timesheets table
2. Verify timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
3. Check timesheet status - allow update only if status is 'pending' or 'rejected'
4. Verify authorization: authenticated user must be timesheet owner OR have time approval permission for organization
5. If timesheet belongs to different organization than user's context, reject with 403
6. Validate request body fields against IHrmPlatformTimesheet.IUpdate schema
7. Only allow update of 'notes' field - other fields are read-only or workflow-controlled
8. Update the timesheet record with new values
9. Update updated_at timestamp to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
10. Return updated full timesheet entity with status, owner details, and timelog count

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: timesheet does not exist or was soft-deleted
- 403 Forbidden: user lacks permission (not owner, no time approval role)
- 409 Conflict: timesheet is in submitted or approved status (locked)
- 400 Bad Request: invalid field values or schema validation failure

Business rules:
- Cannot modify dates once timesheet is created
- Cannot modify status through this endpoint (use submission/rejection workflows)
- Once approved, timelogs are permanently locked
- Notes can be modified at any time while timesheet is in pending or rejected status

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet entity with all fields including status, owner information, timelog count, and timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the timesheet to update. Must be a valid UUID format.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the timesheet. Currently only the notes field can be modified through this operation. Other fields like status, dates, and timesheet totals are controlled by workflow rules and cannot be directly updated.

operations.description:
Delete a timesheet record by setting the soft delete timestamp.

This operation removes a timesheet from active workflows while preserving the record for audit purposes. Employees can delete their own timesheets, subject to timesheet status restrictions: timesheets in approved status cannot be deleted unless the user has time management permission. Users with time:manage permission can delete any employee's timesheets regardless of status.

### Access Control

- **Timesheet Owner**: Can delete their own timesheets if status is pending, submitted, rejected, or cancelled
- **Time Management Users**: Users with time:manage permission can delete any employee's timesheets regardless of status or timesheet ownership

### Error Conditions

- **Unauthorised**: Requesting user is neither the timesheet owner nor has time management permission
- **Timesheet Not Found**: No timesheet exists with the specified ID
- **Timesheet in Approved Status**: Timesheet with approved status cannot be deleted by owner (only time management users can delete approved timesheets)
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate timesheetId is a valid UUID format
2. Query hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE id = timesheetId
3. If record not found, return 404 Not Found with error: "Timesheet not found"
4. Check authorization:
   - Load the employee record from hrm_platform_employees using timesheet.hrm_platform_employee_id
   - If timesheet.hrm_platform_employee_id equals current member's ID (employee), mark as owner-authorized
   - Load current member's role and check if role has time:manage permission
   - If not owner and not has time:manage permission, return 403 Forbidden
5. Check if timesheet is in approved status (status = 'approved'):
   - If approved AND current user is NOT time management user, return 403 Forbidden
   - Approved timesheets can only be deleted by time management users
6. Perform soft delete:
   - Update hrm_platform_timesheets SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE id = timesheetId
   - Cascade delete will automatically remove associated hrm_platform_timesheet_timelogs and hrm_platform_timesheet_actions records (onDelete: Cascade)
7. Return the soft-deleted timesheet record with deleted_at timestamp set
8. Response includes: id, hrm_platform_employee_id, start_date, end_date, status, deleted_at, notes, total_hours

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to delete (UUID format)
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Manages timelogs within a timesheet by adding or removing specific timelog entries from the timesheet collection.

This operation allows employees to modify the timelog composition of a timesheet while it remains in draft status. Timelogs can be added to or removed from the timesheet, enabling employees to curate which work sessions are included in their weekly report.

Status-based access control:
- Draft timesheets: Timelogs can be added or removed freely by the owner
- Submitted/Approved/Rejected timesheets: Timelog modifications are blocked
- Approved timesheets: All timelogs are permanently locked for data integrity

Permission requirements:
- Timesheet owner: Can modify draft timesheets
- Users with time:manage permission: Can modify any timesheet
- Users with time:approve permission: Can only view submitted timesheets
operations.name: manage
operations.specification:
1. Validate timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted
2. Check user permissions:
   - If user is timesheet owner: allow draft modifications
   - If user has time:manage permission: allow all modifications
   - Otherwise: return 403 Forbidden
3. Validate timesheet status:
   - If status is 'submitted', 'approved', or 'rejected': reject with error
   - If status is 'draft': allow modifications
4. Parse request body timelog operations:
   - For 'add' operations: verify timelog exists and is not already in this timesheet
   - For 'remove' operations: verify timelog is currently associated with this timesheet
5. Check timelog approval status:
   - Reject 'add' if timelog is already in an approved timesheet
   - Reject 'remove' if timelog is in an approved timesheet (cannot break approval chain)
6. Create/update timesheet_timelogs junction records:
   - For adds: insert new record with created_at=now()
   - For removes: update deleted_at=now() (soft delete)
7. Recalculate timesheet total_hours:
   - Sum all non-deleted timelogs' duration_minutes
   - Convert to hours (divide by 60)
   - Update timesheet.total_hours
8. Update timesheet updated_at timestamp
9. Return updated timesheet with its timelog collection

Edge cases:
- Empty request body: return 200 with current timesheet state
- Duplicate add operations: skip (idempotent)
- Remove non-existent association: return 200 (no-op)
- Concurrent modifications: use database row-level locking

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet record with its complete timelog collection after applying all operations.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the timesheet containing the timelogs to manage.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Operations to add or remove timelogs from the timesheet. Each operation specifies a timelog UUID and the action to perform.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timelog entry from within a timesheet context, including all work session details, project information, and approval status.

This endpoint returns the complete timelog data including work start/end times, duration, billable status, and associated project and task references. Access control is enforced based on timesheet ownership and user permissions.

Users without time:approve permission can only view timelogs from timesheets they own. Users with time:approve permission can view timelogs from any employee's timesheets. Users with time:manage permission have unrestricted access to all timelogs.

Query the hrm_platform_timelogs table to retrieve a specific timelog entry by ID.

Verification steps:

2. Verify the timelog exists and is associated with the timesheet through hrm_platform_timesheet_timelogs junction table (check deleted_at is NULL)
3. Verify the timelog is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL)

Access control:
- If user owns the timesheet: allow access
- If user has time:approve permission: allow access to any timelog in the organization
- Otherwise: return 403 Forbidden

Once a timesheet is approved, timelogs become immutable. This endpoint should return the timelog data without modification capabilities.

Error cases:

- 403: User lacks permission to view this timelog
- 404: Timelog is soft-deleted

Retrieves all action log records for a specific timesheet to provide complete audit trail visibility.

This endpoint returns all timesheet lifecycle events including submission, approval, and rejection actions. Each record contains the actor who performed the action, timestamp, action type, and optional notes or feedback.

The operation supports filtering by action type and date range, with pagination for efficient browsing of historical audit data.

- date ranges: filter by created_at timestamp

Apply pagination with cursor or offset/limit pattern.

Ensure the requesting user has appropriate permissions to view the timesheet's action history based on their organization membership and role.

Fetches detailed information about a single action in the timesheet lifecycle, including the actor who performed it, the action type (submit/approve/reject), optional notes or feedback, and the timestamp. This endpoint is used to view individual action details within the timesheet audit trail.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific organization's timezone configuration by its unique identifier.

Returns the timezone setting for an organization, which defines the local time reference for all time tracking operations including timer sessions, timelog entries, and timesheet week calculations.

The timezone must be a valid IANA Time Zone Database identifier (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). The system validates the timezone format and rejects invalid identifiers.

Organization data isolation is enforced - users can only access timezone configurations for their currently selected organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Query hrm_platform_time_tracking_timezones table WHERE id = {timezoneId}
2. Validate the requested timezone belongs to the user's currently selected organization (enforce data isolation per organization context from authentication middleware)
3. Check that deleted_at IS NULL (soft delete validation)
4. Return the full timezone configuration record
5. Return 404 Not Found if the timezone configuration does not exist or does not belong to the user's organization
6. Return 404 if the record is soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL)

Implementation notes:
- timezone field must be a valid IANA timezone string (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York')
- The organization_id in the response indicates which organization this configuration belongs to
- No children relationships are included in the response
- The response should include created_at and updated_at timestamps in UTC

operations.description:
Create a timezone configuration for an organization.

Creates a new timezone setting that applies to all time tracking operations within the organization. The timezone determines how dates and times are displayed and calculated for timers, timelogs, and timesheets.

The organization identifier must be unique - each organization can only have one timezone configuration. Attempts to create a second timezone for the same organization will fail with a unique constraint violation.

The timezone field accepts only valid IANA timezone identifiers (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York, Europe/London). Invalid timezone names are rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the provided timezone identifier is a valid IANA timezone name.
2. Check if a timezone configuration already exists for the given organization_id. If found, return unique constraint violation error.
3. Verify the organization exists in hrm_platform_organizations table.
4. Create new timezone configuration record with:
   - Generate UUID for id
   - Set organization_id from request
   - Set timezone from request (validated)
   - Set created_at to current UTC timestamp
   - Set updated_at to current UTC timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to NULL
5. Insert record into hrm_platform_time_tracking_timezones table.
6. Return the created record with all fields.

Error handling:
- UNIQUE constraint violation if organization already has timezone config: 409 Conflict
- Organization not found: 404 Not Found
- Invalid timezone format: 400 Bad Request
- System errors: 500 Internal Server Error

responseBody.description: The newly created timezone configuration record with all fields including the generated ID and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Timezone configuration data including the organization identifier and IANA timezone string. The organization must not already have a timezone configuration.

operations.description:
Update the timezone configuration for an organization.

Updates the IANA timezone identifier used for time calculations across the organization. This setting affects how timer operations, timelogs, and timesheets display and calculate time for all employees in the organization.

The timezone field must be a valid IANA Time Zone Database identifier (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Invalid timezone identifiers are rejected.

Only users with organization management permissions can update timezone settings. The organization context is implicit from the user's current organization selection.

The operation validates that the timezone configuration exists and is not soft-deleted before updating. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time when the update is committed.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the user has organization management permissions (org:manage)
2. Extract organization context from the user's current organization selection
3. Find the timezone configuration record by timezoneId
4. Verify the record exists and deleted_at is NULL (not soft-deleted)
5. Verify the record belongs to the user's organization (organization_id match)
6. Validate the provided timezone format: must be valid IANA timezone identifier
   - Use IANA Time Zone Database validation
   - Reject invalid or custom timezone names
   - Accept formats like 'Area/Location' (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York')
7. Update the timezone field with the provided value
8. Set updated_at to the current timestamp
9. Return the updated timezone configuration record

Edge cases:
- If timezoneId not found: return 404 Not Found
- If record is soft-deleted: return 404 Not Found
- If record belongs to different organization: return 403 Forbidden
- If timezone identifier is invalid: return 400 Bad Request with validation error
- If user lacks organization management permission: return 403 Forbidden

Atomic operations: The update must be atomic - either all changes are committed or none.

operations.description:
Retrieve precomputed weekly timesheet statistics aggregated by employee and week period.

This operation returns paginated results of timesheet weekly statistics for organizations and employees. Each record represents one employee's timesheet activity for a single week (Monday to Sunday), including total hours, billable hours, and counts by timesheet status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected).

### Features

- **Filtering**: Search by organization, employee, week date range, and status counts
- **Pagination**: Cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large result sets
- **Sorting**: Sort results by week_start, total_hours, or employee name
- **Organization Scope**: Results can be filtered by specific organization or include all organizations

### Security

- Organization-level access control: users can only view statistics for their organization unless they have admin privileges
- Employee-specific filtering: users can filter by their own employee_id or manage employee statistics if they have employee:manage permission

### Use Cases

- Dashboard displays showing weekly timesheet summaries
- Administrative reporting on timesheet activity across the organization
- Manager oversight of team members' timesheet submissions
- Payroll and billing preparation using precomputed billable hours
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_timesheet_weekly_stats materialized view with pagination and filtering.

Implementation steps:
1. Apply search filters from requestBody: organization_id (if provided), employee_id (if provided), week_start range (gte/lte), week_end range (gte/lte), and status count filters (draft_timesheet_count, submitted_timesheet_count, approved_timesheet_count, rejected_timesheet_count with range operators)
2. Perform cursor-based pagination: if cursor is provided, use it to fetch the next page; otherwise start from the beginning
3. Apply sorting based on sort field: week_start (default), total_hours, employee name (requires JOIN)
4. Calculate and return pagination metadata: hasNext, hasPrevious, total count (can use COUNT(*) query)
5. Include join with hrm_platform_organizations and hrm_platform_employees for employee name and organization name in the response
6. Order results by week_start DESC (newest weeks first) by default

Edge cases:
- No results: return empty array with pagination metadata showing zero results
- Invalid cursor: treat as new request and start from beginning
- Filter by non-existent employee_id: return empty results
- Filter across organizations: only allow if user has admin:manage permission

Error handling:
- Return 400 for invalid cursor format or invalid date ranges
- Return 403 if user tries to access another organization's data without admin:manage permission
- Return 404 if requested employee_id does not exist (when filtering by specific employee)

Performance considerations:
- Use the composite unique index on (organization_id, employee_id, week_start) for efficient lookups
- Use the (organization_id, week_start) index for organization-scoped filtering
- Consider caching frequently accessed week periods for dashboard performance

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet weekly statistics summary records containing aggregated metrics for each employee and week period, optimized for dashboard displays and administrative reporting.

The statistics are computed and stored in a materialized view for performance. The record is scoped to an organization for multi-tenant data isolation, ensuring employees can only access statistics for their own organization.
